findings.endpoint: plasma concentrations and effectiveness of co-administered drugs
findings.population: patients taking St John's wort with prescription drugs
findings.finding_summary: This review documents clinically significant interactions via induction of CYP3A4 (and CYP2C9, CYP1A2) and P-glycoprotein, reducing concentrations or effect of warfarin, phenprocoumon, cyclosporine, HIV protease inhibitors, theophylline, digoxin, and oral contraceptives — with documented consequences including acute transplant rejection on cyclosporine and breakthrough bleeding and unplanned pregnancies on oral contraceptives.
findings.limitations: the degree of induction is unpredictable across preparations due to variable constituent content

findings.population: pharmacokinetic interaction studies across St John's wort preparations
findings.finding_summary: This review reports that St John's wort preparations activate PXR and induce CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, with the degree of CYP3A4 induction correlating significantly with the preparation's hyperforin content — low-hyperforin preparations carry lower interaction potential.
findings.limitations: hyperforin content is rarely declared on consumer product labels, so users typically cannot apply this distinction

findings.endpoint: serotonin syndrome reports in combination with serotonergic drugs
findings.population: clinical literature on 5-HTP alone and combined with antidepressants
findings.finding_summary: Review-level assessment finds the clinical literature has not documented human serotonin syndrome cases attributed to 5-HTP alone or combined with antidepressants, despite the mechanistic expectation from precursor loading; clinical studies of such combinations generally reported tolerability.
findings.limitations: absence of published case reports is not evidence of safety — the mechanistic risk is real, toxicology guidance advises against combining 5-HTP with SSRIs/MAOIs, and no safe combined dose is established

findings.endpoint: monacolin K content consistency across commercial products
findings.population: 28 red yeast rice supplement brands from mainstream US retailers
findings.finding_summary: Chemical analysis of 28 brands found monacolin K undetectable in two, and among the 26 containing it the content ranged more than 60-fold (0.09 to 5.48 mg per 1,200 mg); following label serving directions, daily monacolin K intake would range more than 120-fold (0.09 to 10.94 mg).
findings.limitations: monacolin K is chemically identical to lovastatin, so this variability means users cannot predict their effective statin dose from the label

findings.finding_summary: In this randomized crossover study, three weeks of hawthorn extract WS 1442 (450 mg twice daily) alongside digoxin 0.25 mg produced no statistically significant changes in any measured digoxin pharmacokinetic parameter, suggesting the combination was safe at these doses.
findings.limitations: eight healthy volunteers and one extract at one dose — a reassuring but narrow negative; clinician oversight is still prudent for heart-failure patients on digoxin

findings.endpoint: biomarker changes in the REDUCE-IT mineral-oil comparator arm
findings.finding_summary: In this REDUCE-IT biomarker substudy, the mineral-oil comparator arm showed 12-month median increases of 21.9% in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, 10.9% in oxidized LDL cholesterol, and 28.9% in interleukin-1beta, reviving debate over whether part of icosapent ethyl's apparent benefit reflects comparator harm; regulatory assessments estimated roughly 3% of the net clinical benefit might be attributable to mineral oil's biomarker effects.
findings.limitations: tempers but does not overturn the primary trial result — the regulatory estimate attributes only a small fraction of the observed benefit to the comparator
